item.title: Specification Portability Across LLM Development Agents: Cross-Agent Compatibility in Specification-Driven Software Migration
item.description: This paper investigates cross-agent specification portability using Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration as a controlled software transformation task. The study combines two experimental stages. First, a specification-first migration pipeline was evaluated on 1,006 PL/SQL files, of which 623 were successfully regenerated and 380 generated scripts executed successfully in PostgreSQL 16. item.title: A2DINOv3: Rethinking Multi-Modal Object Detection via Socialized Collaboration
item.description: Multi-modal object detection is essential for robust scene understanding in challenging conditions, including low-light and adverse environments. item.title: CoAnchor: Robust Collaborative Perception under Spatio-Temporal Misalignment via Object-Level Anchors
item.description: Collaborative perception extends the sensing range of a single vehicle by fusing observations from nearby agents, which improves the robustness of autonomous driving. In realistic deployments, however, the received collaborator messages are often affected by both communication delay and relative-pose noise, which jointly cause stale observations, spatial misalignment, and unstable feature fusion. item.title: Roadside-Cooperative Autonomous Driving: From Data Platform to Vision-Language End-to-End Reasoning
item.description: Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) cooperation enables beyond-line-of-sight perception, mitigating occlusions in single-vehicle sensing. However, existing V2X benchmarks provide limited support for closed-loop evaluation and language-grounded supervision, hindering the development of vision-language models (VLMs) for end-to-end cooperative driving. item.title: WA-JEPA: Rethinking the Video JEPA Paradigm for World-Action Modeling in Autonomous Driving
item.description: Video Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (V-JEPA) learns powerful spatiotemporal representations from video through self-supervised latent feature prediction. However, V-JEPA is built around random-mask completion and deterministic regression, making it fundamentally ill-suited for autonomous driving planning that demands future-directed prediction tightly coupled with action. item.description: Bimanual manipulation enables complex tasks but introduces added complexity from the high number of degrees of freedom involved. When handling rigid objects, the relative transformation between the two end effectors must remain fixed throughout the motion, manifesting as a nonlinear equality constraint that confines the feasible configuration space to a measure-zero manifold and challenges conventional motion planners. item.title: A Safety-Driven Architectural Framework for Fail-Operational Drone Swarms in Critical Missions
item.description: The certification of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms for safety-critical operations requires verifiable design assurance. Airworthiness standards demand deterministic reliability, whereas multi-agent coordination algorithms execute non-deterministic models. item.title: A Collaborative Multi-Modality Interaction for VLA-based End-to-End Autonomous Driving
item.description: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a powerful paradigm for end-to-end autonomous driving by jointly integrating perception, reasoning, and decision making within a unified multimodal framework. item.title: Multi-Modal Traffic Sign Detection with Semantic Attributes for Autonomous Driving
item.description: Reliable traffic sign detection is a prerequisite for the global deployment of autonomous driving systems, where regulatory compliance and road safety depend on perceiving signs correctly across regions, ranges, and weather conditions. item.title: Fine-tuning LLMs for Tourist Trajectory Prediction using Field Experiment Data
item.description: Evaluating mobility interventions at tourist destinations requires predicting visitor behavior under varying conditions. item.title: Structure for Reading, Prose for Writing: Asymmetric Structural Conditioning in Multi-Agent Document Authoring
item.description: Multi-agent pipelines that author formal documents must both read a requester's forms and write against them. item.title: Vis-Poison: Poisoning Visual Knowledge in Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
item.description: While multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems increasingly rely on images as external knowledge sources, the introduction of poisoned visual evidence can severely compromise multimodal large language model (MLLM) generation. item.title: Dual-Cache Latent Space Communication between Heterogeneous Language Models
item.description: Multi-agent LLM systems split work across models, so answering often requires knowledge that sits in another agent's context: a Sharer has encoded information that a Receiver needs to complete its task. item.title: Consilience: Conformally Calibrated Communication Control for Hidden-Profile Multi-Agent Reasoning
item.description: Multi-agent LLM systems can improve reasoning by pooling diverse perspectives, but their effectiveness depends on coordinating communication, particularly in hidden-profile settings where each agent holds only part of the evidence required for a correct decision. item.title: FL-MAESTRO: Multi-Agent LLM Orchestration for Resource-Constrained Federated Learning
item.description: In Federated Learning (FL), the communication topology is a runtime variable rather than a fixed design choice, since links and edge devices drop in and out during training. item.title: Towards Traffic Modelling of Multi-Agent Systems: The Role of Coordination Topology
